module_name: Early Adulthood in Vienna and Munich

extracted_notes.text:
In 1907, Hitler left Linz to live and study fine art in Vienna, financed by an orphan's benefits and support from his mother. He applied for admission to the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna but was rejected twice. The director suggested Hitler should apply to the School of Architecture, but he lacked the necessary academic credentials because he had not finished secondary school.
On 21 December 1907, his mother died of breast cancer at the age of 47; Hitler was 18 at the time. In 1909, Hitler ran out of money and was forced to live a bohemian life in homeless shelters and the Meldemannstrasse dormitory. He earned money as a casual labourer and by painting and selling watercolours of Vienna's sights. During his time in Vienna, he pursued a growing passion for architecture and music, attending ten performances of Lohengrin, his favourite of Richard Wagner's operas.

Hitler received the final part of his father's estate in May 1913 and moved to Munich. When he was conscripted into the Austro-Hungarian Army, he journeyed to Salzburg on 5 February 1914 for medical assessment. After he was deemed unfit for service, he returned to Munich. Hitler later claimed that he did not wish to serve the Habsburg Empire because of the mixture of races in its army and his belief that the collapse of Austria-Hungary was imminent.

In Vienna, Hitler was first exposed to racist rhetoric. Populists such as mayor Karl Lueger exploited the city's prevalent antisemitic sentiment, occasionally also espousing German nationalist notions for political benefit. German nationalism was especially widespread in the Mariahilf district, where Hitler then lived. Georg Ritter von Schonerer became a major influence on Hitler, and he developed an admiration for Martin Luther.
Hitler read newspapers and pamphlets that promoted prejudice and warned of an influx of Eastern European Jews, as well as writings by figures such as Houston Stewart Chamberlain, Charles Darwin, Friedrich Nietzsche, Gustave Le Bon, and Arthur Schopenhauer. During his years in Vienna he also developed strong anti-Slavic sentiments.

cast_of_characters.core_contribution: His writings were consumed by Hitler as he developed his antisemitic and anti-Slavic sentiments.

cast_of_characters.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
cast_of_characters.core_contribution: One of the several thinkers whose works Hitler read during his formative years in Vienna.

legacy_impact.relevance_statement: Studying these formative years reveals how personal failure, social instability, and the presence of toxic populist rhetoric can combine to create a catalyst for extreme ideology and global catastrophe.

cards.parent_topic: Early Adulthood in Vienna and Munich

blocks.text_content: In **1907**, Adolf Hitler left Linz to live and study fine art in **Vienna**. His journey was financed by his mother and orphan's benefits, marking the beginning of a period of transition and personal loss.

fact_grid_data.title: Early Life Timeline
fact_grid_data.intro_text: Key dates and milestones from Hitler's early adulthood as he moved between major cities and faced personal loss.

blocks.text_content: However, his dreams of becoming an artist were met with immediate obstacles, leading to a series of setbacks that would reshape his life.

cards.parent_topic: Early Adulthood in Vienna and Munich

blocks.text_content: Hitler's artistic dreams were quickly dashed when he applied to the **Academy of Fine Arts Vienna**. He was rejected twice, leaving him without a clear path forward in the art world.

flip_reveal_data.front_text: Why did the director of the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna suggest Hitler apply to the School of Architecture?
flip_reveal_data.back_text: Because he was rejected twice from the Academy of Fine Arts, and the director suggested architecture as an alternative, though he lacked the academic credentials to be admitted.

blocks.text_content: This professional setback was soon followed by a devastating personal blow: on **21 December 1907**, his mother died of breast cancer at the age of 47.

cards.parent_topic: Early Adulthood in Vienna and Munich

blocks.text_content: By **1909**, Hitler's financial resources had vanished, forcing him into a precarious, bohemian lifestyle.

stepper_data.intro_text: A chronological sequence of events during Adolf Hitler's time in Vienna from 1907 to 1909.
steps: 1907: Moved to Vienna to study fine art.
Rejected twice by the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.
1909: Ran out of money and lived in homeless shelters and the Meldemannstrasse dormitory.

fact_grid_data.title: Hitler's Time in Vienna
fact_grid_data.intro_text: During his years in Vienna, Hitler lived a bohemian existence characterized by financial struggle and a pursuit of artistic interests.

items.label: Residence
items.value: Homeless shelters and the Meldemannstrasse dormitory

blocks.text_content: While struggling to make ends meet, he immersed himself in the city's cultural landscape. But Vienna offered more than just art; it was also where he first encountered the rhetoric that would define his future.

cards.parent_topic: Early Adulthood in Vienna and Munich

blocks.text_content: Vienna was a city rife with antisemitic sentiment, which was frequently exploited by populists like mayor **Karl Lueger**. Living in the **Mariahilf district**, Hitler was immersed in an environment where German nationalism was widespread.

branching_tree_data.title: Influences on Hitler's Ideology in Vienna
branching_tree_data.intro_text: During his time in Vienna, Hitler was exposed to various political, religious, and intellectual figures whose ideas shaped his developing worldview.
branching_tree_data.root: Influences on Hitler's Ideology in Vienna

branches.label: Political Figures
branches.definition: Populists like mayor Karl Lueger and figures such as Georg Ritter von Schonerer who promoted racist rhetoric and German nationalism.

branches.label: Religious/Historical Figures
branches.definition: Hitler developed an admiration for Martin Luther during his years in Vienna.

branches.label: Authors/Thinkers
branches.definition: Hitler read writings by Houston Stewart Chamberlain, Charles Darwin, Friedrich Nietzsche, Gustave Le Bon, and Arthur Schopenhauer.

blocks.text_content: Beyond the intellectual influences of the time, he consumed pamphlets and newspapers that warned of an influx of Eastern European Jews and developed strong anti-Slavic sentiments. These formative years in Vienna ended in May 1913, when he received the final part of his father's estate and moved to Munich.

cards.parent_topic: Early Adulthood in Vienna and Munich

blocks.text_content: In Munich, Hitler's life took another turn when he was conscripted into the **Austro-Hungarian Army**. He traveled to Salzburg in **February 1914** for a medical assessment, but he was ultimately deemed unfit for service.

insight_badge_data.expanded_detail: Hitler claimed he avoided serving in the Habsburg Empire's army due to its mixture of races and his belief that the collapse of Austria-Hungary was imminent.

blocks.text_content: This intersection of medical assessment and ideological disdain for the multi-ethnic Habsburg Empire left him in a state of transition, awaiting the catalyst that would fundamentally alter his trajectory.
